clue.text: Women, mature, for hire

blocks.note: W is the standard abbreviation for women
to age is to mature or grow older

explanation.surface: A recruitment notice offering work to grown-up women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For hire' reads as one phrase, but 'for' is only the link and 'hire' is a noun meaning payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Hire in its older sense is the payment given for labour, which is a synonym of pay or wage.

clue.text: One lacking entry permit we support when it's shortly acquired

indicators.note: what is acquired is taken in, so one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: WE plus BACK, to support
'it' in its shortened form, as in 'twas, is 'T

explanation.surface: An immigrant without papers is backed by a group once the paperwork is quickly obtained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It shortly' means the clipped form 'T found in 'tis and 'twas. Wetback is a derogatory American term for an illegal immigrant from Mexico, originally one who swam the Rio Grande.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang term names a migrant who crossed into the US illegally, i.e. without any right of entry.

clue.text: Police abroad, ideal when following car or lorry up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the word from bottom to top

blocks.note: drag is slang for a car, and also a heavy vehicle for hauling
A1 means first-rate, with the 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Foreign police find it ideal to follow a vehicle up the road.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 written as AI is a common crossword device. The Gardai (Garda Síochána) are the police force of the Irish Republic.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardai is the plural of garda, an Irish police officer, so it is police in a country abroad.

clue.text: Giant of old among men or mice

indicators.note: among says the letters sit within the run of words that follows

blocks.note: letters spanning the three words

explanation.surface: A giant from legend stands among ordinary creatures, men and mice alike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Giant' looks like a noun, but here it is the adjective, and enorm is an obsolete form of enormous.
explanation.definitionFit: Enorm is an archaic adjective meaning huge or enormous, which is what giant means as an adjective.

clue.text: Wine the French bottled in torrent

indicators.note: something bottled is held inside a vessel, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a spate is a sudden flood
les is French for 'the' in the plural

explanation.surface: French wine is bottled during a downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: Spätlese is a German late-harvest white wine, a specific example of wine.

clue.text: English Pernod I spit out swallowing it? it's bad for the heart

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are disordered, set wrong
swallowing takes something inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
E is the abbreviation for English
Ricard is a pastis made by the Pernod Ricard company, i.e. a Pernod-style drink

explanation.surface: Someone spits out an aniseed drink, perhaps because drinking it harms the heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it?' refers back to the drink, the E plus RICARD swallowed by the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Pericarditis is inflammation of the membrane around the heart, a condition harmful to it.

clue.text: Matlo sails it at sea – masthead flies from this?

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: a matlo is slang for a sailor; the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor takes to the ocean, flying a flag from the masthead.
explanation.walkthrough: Alt altissimo is the very highest musical pitch, the top register above altissimo; the definition jokes that a masthead, the highest point of a ship, flies from this height.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase denotes the very highest point, and the question mark marks the playful link to a ship's topmost position.

clue.text: Where cattle are kept warm and dry, gale swirling outside

indicators.note: swirling letters are whirled around into a new order
outside says these letters wrap around the other piece

blocks.note: to air clothes is to warm and dry them
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Livestock are sheltered warm and dry while a storm rages outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A lairage is a place where cattle are rested or penned, for example on the way to market or slaughter.

clue.text: Brit leader's abandoned, astray?

blocks.note: brit are young herring
the first letter, the one to be removed

explanation.surface: A British party leader has been deserted and gone off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brit' looks like a Briton, but it is a young herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Erring means straying from the right path, so someone erring has gone astray.

clue.text: Wherein biological populations are preserved – conditions including lab I fitted out

indicators.note: fitted out suggests refitting and rearranging the parts
including means holding something within

blocks.note: states are conditions
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Describes a laboratory freezer kept in suitable conditions for storing organisms.
explanation.definitionFit: Stabilates are samples of microorganisms preserved alive, typically frozen, so a population is stored unchanged.

clue.text: Cornish visitor, one with good vision letting go of rope

indicators.note: letting go means releasing something, so these letters are dropped

blocks.note: an emmetrope has normal eyesight, needing no glasses
taken as written, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: A sharp-eyed tourist in Cornwall drops a rope.
explanation.walkthrough: Emmet is Cornish dialect for an ant and, by extension, a tourist swarming into Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cornwall a holidaymaker is nicknamed an emmet, local dialect for an ant.

clue.text: Service book, one lying behind e.g. main part of church, from east to west

behind places the one lying after the church words, so it comes second in the answer

the nave is the main body of a church
a liar is one telling lies

explanation.surface: A prayer book is found where someone lies at the back of a church nave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' places the liar after the reversed letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An evangeliar is a liturgical book of the Gospel passages read at services.

clue.text: Bobby on Thursday beat

blocks.note: TH is an abbreviation of Thursday

explanation.surface: A British policeman (a bobby) walks his beat on Thursday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bobby' suggests a policeman and 'beat' his patrol, but Bobby is a name, with Rob another nickname for Robert; 'on' puts it after Thursday.
explanation.definitionFit: To throb is to pulse rhythmically, the same as a heart that beats.

clue.text: Moravian, German gent, Jaeger, name becoming leader

indicators.note: becoming leader means a letter leaves its place and goes to the front instead

blocks.note: Herr is German for Mr or gentleman
N is the abbreviation for name
Jäger is German for hunter

explanation.surface: A list of German descriptions: a Moravian man, a gentleman, a Jaeger.
explanation.walkthrough: The N is taken out of its place in the hunter word and put at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Herrnhuter is a name for a member of the Moravian Church, after its community at Herrnhut in Saxony.

clue.text: Bit of foreign money I put into drink

indicators.note: putting something into another places it inside

blocks.note: a dram is a small measure of spirits
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone slips a foreign coin into their glass.
explanation.definitionFit: The diram is a small coin, a hundredth of the Tajik somoni and a fraction of other Middle Eastern currencies.

clue.text: Speech, a hit with bride, thrilled, husband delivered

thrilled suggests being stirred up and agitated, so the letters move

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for husband, the letter removed

clue.text: Edible weed, sweet, removed from wrapping

clue.text: Shut up in prison, one given time (5, two words)

blocks.note: the can is slang for prison
the Roman numeral for one
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A convict locked in jail is handed a sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shut up in prison' reads as one phrase about confinement, but 'Shut up' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Can it is a slang command to stop talking, the same as telling someone to be quiet.

clue.text: Carpet is woven with wavy edge

indicators.note: weaving interlaces threads into a new pattern, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rug has been woven with a rippled border.
explanation.definitionFit: Crispate is a botanical term for leaves or margins that are curled or crimped, i.e. wavy along the edge.

clue.text: Show more inclination to guide writer having run away

indicators.note: something that has run away has gone, so its letter is removed

blocks.note: to steer is to guide
R is the cricket abbreviation for run, the letter removed
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: Someone is more willing to lead an author who has escaped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inclination' suggests willingness, but here it means slope.
explanation.definitionFit: To steepen is to become steeper, that is, to slope more sharply, showing more inclination in the physical sense.

clue.text: Hull? That's involved with North Sea mostly

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed
mostly means not all, so the final letter is cut

blocks.note: the definition word reused as letters
N is the abbreviation for north
taken as written, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: Asks whether the port of Hull is involved with the North Sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hull' is both the definition and part of the letters to rearrange. Hull is an English port city on the North Sea coast.
explanation.definitionFit: To hull peas or nuts is to remove their outer case, which is what unshell means.

clue.text: Travelling box one's packed in Jordanian destination?

indicators.note: packed in means put inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: Petra is the ancient rock city in Jordan, a tourist destination
A means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: A trunk for a journey is packed for a trip to Jordan.
explanation.definitionFit: A petara is an Indian box or basket for carrying clothes on a journey.

clue.text: One dressing offal having to call back after lapse

blocks.note: a trip is a slip or lapse
to call someone something is to name them

explanation.surface: A butcher dressing a carcass must ring back after a slip-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripeman prepares and sells tripe, the cleaned stomach lining of cattle, which is offal.

clue.text: Object of worship I wrapped in loose gown

blocks.note: a manto is a loose cloak or mantle
taken as written

clue.text: One of a pair connected in vice, creating frightful noise behind church

definitions.text: One of a pair connected in vice

indicators.note: behind sends the frightful noise to the rear, after the church abbreviation

clue.text: Ball penetrating one side of wicket, turning? I must get even
